text:
sam: Heads-up: found a parity + typing bug between sync/async Python streaming in the SDK. Sync iterator sometimes yields an empty string chunk and then stops when a retry happens mid-stream. Async iterator keeps going. Breaks apps that expect the stream to be continuous.

sam: Repro sketch: use tcpkill to drop packets mid-SSE, or emulate a 502 response in the middle of a multi-chunk response.

sam: Minimal pseudo repro:
```python
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=...)
stream = client.chat.stream([{"role":"user","content":"start"}])
for chunk in stream:
    # sometimes get '' then StopIteration, even though server later sends more
    print(repr(chunk))
```

sam: Observed: chunk == '' OR chunk == b'' then iterator stops. The SDK later reconnects and receives remaining tokens, but the caller already exited the loop.

lee: That's nasty. Does this only happen for SSE/chunked body? Any model-specific behavior?

sam: Only seen on streaming responses (SSE/chunked). Non-stream endpoints unaffected. Happens with redwood-sdk==0.13.0, python 3.10 & 3.11.

mike: Two issues: 1) typing inconsistency (stubs declare Iterator[str] but code sometimes yields bytes), 2) generator lifecycle/stop semantics when retrying. Both need fixes.

alexa: Agree. We should not signal completion by yielding an empty chunk. Either normalize empty frames (ignore) or buffer until final close. Also sync and async impls must match.

sam: Quick workaround for app-level: use an explicit drain loop and re-open stream if you see termination without EOF marker, but that's ugly.

lee: For a short patch: make decoder always return str (utf-8 decode) and treat empty bytes as "skip" unless server explicitly sends an EOF event. Add a flag like `allow_reconnect=True` on stream objects to keep generator open across retries.

mike: Caveat: server could legitimately send a zero-length payload (rare). Better to rely on explicit SSE "event: done" or connection close. But we control our server so we can add an explicit final event easily.

alexa: Can someone open a ticket w/ repro steps + tcpkill command + minimal harness? We'll triage and mark P2. I'll also add an integration test that splits chunks at arbitrary boundaries to avoid depending on OS-level packet drops.

sam: Created ticket DEVEX-3198 (placeholder): includes harness and tcpkill example. Added logs.

dev-bot: Ticket DEVEX-3198 created and assigned to @alexa. Priority: P2.

mike: I'll push a small test and a types update in stubs/pyi: change Iterator[str] -> Iterator[Union[str, bytes]] for now or normalize to str and bump minor version. Prefer normalize to str and document migration.

alexa: Plan: (1) short-term patch: filter empty chunks and normalize to str in both sync/async, (2) medium: change generator to not close on transient network errors and tie retry state to iterator lifetime, (3) long-term: add exhaustive parity tests for sync/async.

lee: Assign me for integ test failures. I can run tcpkill harness and validate across py3.9-3.11.

sam: TY. Also adding a note in upgrade guide about typing change and behavior.

alexa: Closing loop: we'll land the short-term fix today and follow up with the middle changes. If you hit this, please drop your repro in DEVEX-3198. :thumbsup:
